principalConclusion: ARA UX is task- and question-oriented, mobile-first and progressively disclosed. Chat/MCP performs bounded semantic operations while ARA makes targets, artifacts, versions, comments, diffs, authority, sync and publication visible and deterministically controllable. Offline, failure, permission and unavailable-capability states are first-class.
acceptedDecisions: Use one primary task per mobile view and optional contextual panes on desktop.
Represent profiles and overlays before advanced parameter fields.
Show effective semantic diff and whether a change is runtime, content or composition.
Use placements/revisions/provenance explicitly while keeping database/storage internals hidden.
Separate audit, repair, approval and publication screens/actions.
Use question-oriented analytics and no universal dashboard.
Provide non-drag/list alternatives for composition graphs and two-dimensional resources.
Adopt design tokens, WCAG 2.2 AA target and en/pt-BR/pt-PT message keys.
Require comprehension/accessibility/device evaluation before product implementation.

Issue9: Map every release slice to approved screen IDs, journeys, domain objects, ADRs and quality gates.
Create implementation issues only when all required screens/states for the slice are included.
Include accessibility/localization/offline/failure tests in Definition of Done.
